name: 06_usage_feeder_sum_order
description: Cross-core guard on the budget FEEDER's two summation orders — the ONLY vector that drives raw usage → reduce_sum → aggregate_usage (the price kind feeds measured directly and bypasses both). One pool `shared` is fed by THREE options a,b,c of disparate magnitude, written in INSERTION order c,b,a (≠ the sorted a,b,c). Each option draws across THREE instances j0,j1,j2 with the BIG draw written FIRST (j0), so the feeder's insertion order (j0,j1,j2) differs from the ascending-value order — exercising reduce_sum's instance-sum order. Per-option ascending sums: a=1+1+1e16, b=2+3+4=9, c=5+6+1e15. aggregate_usage then sums those per-option totals in NAME order (a,b,c): ((1e16+2)+9)+(1e15+7) = 11000000000000024 exactly. IEEE-754 addition is non-associative, so a core that summed instances or options in any other order (e.g. the old TS Map-insertion order, or summing the 1e16 draw before the small ones) would land a DIFFERENT bit pattern (proven: insertion-order sums differ by 2 ULP). With step α=1 and cap 0 the single tick gives λ_shared = 1·(11000000000000024-0) = 11000000000000024 (an exact integer chosen so the literal round-trips identically through both JSON parsers). Published as the shared budget:shared weight, option `a` (draws 1 unit, financial 0) scores λ; competitor `rival` is priced financial=11000000000000024 (== λ) so the two tie and break by name → [a, rival]. Any divergence in either summation order changes measured → λ → the tie, flipping the queue. Captured from the live aggregate_usage→tick→publish→resolve on both cores.
